title: Lossy-binding with quantized kernels causing sporadic crashloops — recovery plan and follow-ups
creator: Priya Nair
summary: A subset of customer workloads experienced recurring crash loops and degraded accuracy after the int8-kernel binding change. Root cause traces to a nondeterministic binding path where quantized weight metadata lost precision ("lossy-binding") and the kernel selector fell back to incompatible op variants under load. This ticket captures the incident timeline, mitigation, and action items to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-18 22:07 UTC and 2026-02-19 04:12 UTC we observed ~62k failed inferences across 3 tenants using dedicated capacity. Failures surfaced as runtime crash loops on serving pods and >15% increase in retry latencies for impacted routes. One customer reported production feature degradation for a multi-turn chat flow (SEC-ACCT-231).

root_cause: The kernel-selection change introduced a binding heuristic that prefers quantized kernels based on per-weight metadata heuristics. Under concurrent batching and prefix KV cache reuse, a rounding/truncation bug in the weight metadata serializer caused small precision shifts in the quantization scales (lossy-binding). That shift triggered an accidental match with an operator variant that assumed a different dequantization order, producing invalid memory accesses and crash loops. The failure mode is nondeterministic at low load and amplified under the dedicated pool's continuous batching patterns.
mitigation: Immediate rollback of the canary change and hotpatch to pin the selector to verified kernel candidates. Added runtime guardrails to abort kernel bind when metadata checksum mismatch detected. Increased observability: dumping binding decisions into traces and adding an alert on sudden restart rate increases in dedicated pools.

ENG-27944-A3: Harden kernel-selector to verify dequant order compatibility before binding; fail open to interpreter when uncertainty detected (owner: Evan Mitchell) — estimate 5 pts — due 2026-03-18
ENG-27944-A4: Run synthetic soak on dedicated pools for 48h with new guards; monitor restarts and accuracy drift (owner: SRE team lead - Nora Liu) — estimate 2 pts — due 2026-03-20
ENG-27944-A5: Create a rollout playbook for kernel selector changes including automatic canary rollback window and kill-switch (owner: On-call rotation) — estimate 2 pts — due 2026-03-15

notes: Trade-off: checksum adds a tiny CPU overhead on model load; acceptable for safety-critical tenants and default for dedicated pools. Consider opt-out flag for very latency-sensitive workloads.
Decision: prefer detection and safe fail-open to interpreter rather than forcing fallback kernels that may be incompatible.
Follow-up: evaluate recording of kernel-binding telemetry for 30d to detect near-miss mismatches and accuracy drifts.
Related: see ENG-15842 for prior kernel-selection drift mitigations; reuse parts of that test harness.
